```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(
  collapse = TRUE,
  comment = "#>",
  fig.width = 8,
  fig.height = 4.5
)
```

The examples below complete a short workflow: run predeclared models, read the
saved results as tables, and draw a performance plot. The data are synthetic;
they illustrate software behavior, not clinical usefulness or external validity.

`result_table()` and `plot_perf()` only read saved results. They do
not train, tune, recalibrate, recompute metrics, or select a winning model.

## Binary prediction: two models on the same folds

```{r binary-run}
library(stormbreaker)
d <- bi_example(n = 60, seed = 1)
task <- bi_task(
  d, "patient_id", "outcome", c("gene_a", "gene_b")
)
compared <- compare_cv(
  task,
  list(
    sb_pipeline(learner = "logistic"),
    sb_pipeline(learner = "gaussian_naive_bayes")
  ),
  folds = 3,
  seed = 1
)
```

### Read a metric table

```{r binary-table}
result_table(compared, metric = "roc_auc")
```

Each row represents one supplied pipeline. These columns answer different
questions:

| Column | Meaning |
|:--|:--|
| `estimate` | The original saved value, including missing or infinite values |
| `status` | Whether this particular metric is evaluable |
| `run_status` | Whether the complete CV run succeeded |
| `scope` | Which observations/comparisons the metric describes |
| `aggregation` | How the saved metric combines its contributions |

For binary ROC AUC, comparisons are within outer assessment folds, with the
saved pair-based aggregation. This is **not** a new pooled ROC AUC calculation
across predictions from different fitted folds. Average precision also keeps
its saved fold-aware definition; it is not relabeled as interpolated PR AUC.

Other supported binary choices are:

```{r binary-other-metrics}
result_table(compared, metric = "average_precision")
result_table(compared, metric = "brier_score")
result_table(compared, metric = "log_loss")
```

### Draw the first performance plot

Plotting needs the optional package `ggplot2`. If it is absent, install it with
`install.packages("ggplot2")`; tables and model fitting do not need it.

```{r binary-plot}
if (requireNamespace("ggplot2", quietly = TRUE)) {
  print(plot_perf(compared, "roc_auc"))
}
```

Models appear top-to-bottom in the original input order, not performance order.
Only finite estimates from successful metrics **and** successful complete runs
are drawn. A method without a point still has an axis label. The caption counts
these methods; the metric table supplies their separate statuses.

There are no confidence intervals in this plot. Fold-to-fold variability is not
silently turned into a confidence interval. Selecting the highest observed
development score and reporting it as an unbiased winner is not supported.

## Patient predictions and run records

```{r binary-details}
head(result_table(compared, "predictions"))
result_table(compared, "runs")
```

These tables preserve saved columns and add `task_type`. Each pipeline retains
its own patient predictions, so patient IDs legitimately recur across pipelines.
Use the pipeline and patient columns together; do not treat rows from several
models as independent patients. Output row names are reset and are not IDs.

The run table retains existing `error_class` and `error_message` fields. A stage
is not guessed from the wording of an old error. If one method fails, its row
does not disappear and its estimate is not filled with zero or another model's
prediction. Inspect both the metric table and run records.

Default performance plots show only successful, finite metrics from successful
runs, without empty method labels. `show_unavailable = TRUE` restores the
diagnostic display. If none are usable, the plot says so rather than implying
a successful analysis. `sb_failure_table(compared)` extracts saved issues;
`sb_export_failures(compared, "new-failures.csv")` writes a separate CSV with
cohort, pipeline, stage, fold, metric, status and saved reason. Review original
error text before sharing. Model-dependent failures remain recorded while
later valid pipelines continue; no fallback model is substituted.

**Patient tables can include identifiers and outcomes.** Review them before
sharing; no export or automatic patient-level report is performed here.

## Survival prediction

```{r survival-run}
s <- surv_example(n = 60, seed = 1)
survival_task <- surv_task(
  s, "patient_id", "time", "event", c("gene_a", "gene_b"), "month"
)
survival_result <- run_cv(survival_task, folds = 3, seed = 1)
result_table(survival_result, metric = "harrell_c")
head(result_table(survival_result, "predictions"))
result_table(survival_result, "runs")
```

```{r survival-plot}
if (requireNamespace("ggplot2", quietly = TRUE)) {
  print(plot_perf(survival_result, "harrell_c"))
}
```

Harrell C keeps its saved within-fold comparisons and summed-comparable-pair
aggregation. A single saved CV result is accepted, as is a shared-fold
comparison of survival pipelines. These results remain development CV results;
plotting does not turn them into external validation.

## Read saved fixed-horizon survival metrics

```{r survival-horizon-metrics}
horizon_task <- surv_task(
  s, "patient_id", "time", "event", "gene_a", "month",
  prediction_horizon = 6
)
horizon_result <- run_cv(horizon_task, folds = 3, seed = 1)
for (metric in c("time_auc", "uno_c", "ipcw_brier")) {
  print(result_table(horizon_result, metric = metric))
}
if (requireNamespace("ggplot2", quietly = TRUE)) {
  print(plot_perf(horizon_result, "ipcw_brier"))
}
```

These are the saved cumulative/dynamic time-AUC, truncated Uno C and IPCW
Brier estimate, not a new calculation. Each table retains the horizon and
time unit. Plot labels keep different targets distinct, without conversion or
pooling. The weighted Brier estimate may exceed one and is not clipped.

## Scope of the result-view interface

- Supported objects: single binary/survival CV, shared-fold CV comparisons,
  external evaluations and single-cohort external comparisons.
- Supported scalar metrics: binary `roc_auc`, `average_precision`,
  `brier_score`, `log_loss`, and survival `harrell_c`, `time_auc`, `uno_c`,
  `ipcw_brier`.
- Explicitly choose a metric for a metric table. Do not pass `metric` when
  requesting predictions or run records.
- The three fixed-horizon metrics return `not_requested` and `NA` if absent
  from a successful horizon-free result, or `not_saved` if absent otherwise.
  Other unsupported/missing requests retain explicit errors. No missing metric
  is computed on demand.
- Nested reference/skill scores and feature stability keep their detailed
  objects. Calibration and decision curves have dedicated plot functions.
- Whole repeated CV, IECV and stacking CV now retain separate saved-entry
  contexts in tables, plots, reports and failure exports, without pooling.
- The existing full workflow vignette explains final fitting and outcome-blind
  external evaluation. This tutorial adds result reading, not a replacement
  model-development framework.

Plots are ordinary `ggplot` objects that can be customized and saved explicitly.
For many long pipeline labels, use a taller output image or display a smaller,
predeclared candidate set. No files are written by the plotting function itself.

## Whole composite results

Tables, performance/calibration/DCA plots, reports and failure exports accept
whole repeated CV, IECV and stacking CV results. Context columns identify
`repeat_id`, `heldout_cohort_id`, `model_role`, `validation_scheme` and `view_id`.
A `view_id` identifies a structural saved entry, not a patient. Existing
pipeline IDs remain unchanged. Repeated stacks retain member/stack roles.
IECV is method-development validation, not final independent external
validation. No averaging or pooling across repeats or cohorts is performed.

```{r composite-saved-results}
composite_data <- bi_example(60, seed = 5)
composite_task <- bi_task(
  composite_data, "patient_id", "outcome", "gene_a"
)
composite_result <- sb_compare_repeated_cv(
  composite_task, list(sb_pipeline(learner = "logistic")),
  folds = 3, seeds = c(1, 2)
)
result_table(composite_result, metric = "roc_auc")
sb_failure_table(composite_result)
if (requireNamespace("ggplot2", quietly = TRUE)) {
  plot_perf(composite_result, "roc_auc")
}
```

Pass the same whole object to `sb_render_report()` with a new HTML filename;
each saved leaf gets a separate section. Pass a native `sb_run_stack_cv()` or
`sb_run_internal_external_cv()` result in exactly the same way. Stack views
show outer-CV members and the stack, not inner training folds. Failed entries
remain in tables and failure exports; default plots omit unavailable entries.
Different survival horizons and units remain distinct targets.
